description: Permission in Principle: Development of site to provide 1no. dwelling
decision_conditions:
<ol style="margin-top:0cm" start="1" type="1">
 </ol><p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-family:
     &quot;Arial&quot;,sans-serif">The proposed development, by reason of its siting and
     encroachment on private rear garden area, would constitute Garden Land
     Development and would be at odds with the Councils spatial strategy for
     growth, to the detriment of the character and appearance of the locality
     and the contribution that gardens make to the character of the area, and
     the implementation of sustainable growth within the Borough, contrary to
     Core policies CS1.A and CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and the
     adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Garden Land Development (2013).<o:p></o:p></span></p><ol style="margin-top:0cm" start="1" type="1">
</ol>

<p>The proposed development, due to its poor location given the adjacent land uses and elevated railway tracks, loss of adequate amenity space from 19B Abercorn Crescent, limited access, poor quality and incongruous setting, and impacts on the amenities of neighbouring properties, &nbsp;would result in a cramped and contrived form of development which would not provide a high standard of functionality or residential accommodation to meet the needs of future occupiers, adequate amenity provision for future or neighbouring occupiers, or &nbsp;a high standard of design. The application site is therefore considered to be highly inappropriate for a residential development and therefore the proposed location and land use are unacceptable. The proposal is thereby contrary to the high-quality design aspirations of The National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies D3.A, D3.D, D6, D13 and D14 of The London Plan (2021), core policy CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and policies DM1 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).</p>
